<reason>A more convincingly separated the benefits of subsidy reform from the justification for a uniform five-year deadline. Its conditional alternative captured some savings while addressing exclusion and unreliable delivery. B established substantial costs of delay, but did not adequately justify proceeding when compensation still fails. A directly answered the certification challenge and acknowledged temporary leakage. B also incorrectly alleged unanswered questions before A’s scheduled response and invoked a nonexistent reference, weakening its rebuttal credibility.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s answer to “We proceed” exposed the central gap: gradual price increases and years of registry-building do not compensate a household the system still misses. B treated exclusion as manageable underpayment; A showed why those are materially different risks.</best_rebuttal>
